text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.7% today, dropping $9.64 from Friday's close. The main driver was a sharp decline in crude oil prices—down for a second straight day as markets bet on a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict rather than further escalation. Oil prices matter directly to an integrated oil company's profits: lower crude means lower revenue from production, even if refining margins might improve slightly from cheaper input costs.

The stock has been volatile this past week, surging $7 on Friday (when geopolitical tensions seemed to be rising) before giving back most of those gains today. A Democratic sweep in the midterms, now looking likely, could also weigh on energy stocks longer-term—Democratic-controlled Congress typically favors renewable energy investment and stricter fossil fuel policies—though today's move appears driven mainly by the immediate shift in oil market sentiment away from supply disruption fears.
